questions.stem: Which of the following defines Specified Duties of a Non-Commissioned Officer?
questions.key: Duties related to jobs and positions
distractors: Duties not specified as part of a job position or MOS, or other-directed
Duties that often support specified duties but may not be related to the MOS job position
Duties that refer to collective or organizational accountability
questions.explanation: Slide 22 lists three types of NCO duties; specified duties are those related to jobs and positions.
why: That describes directed duties.
That describes implied duties.
Collective accountability describes command responsibility, a category of responsibility, not a type of duty.

questions.stem: These are duties that often support specified duties but, in some cases, may not be related to the MOS job position.
questions.explanation: Implied duties often support specified duties, even when not tied to the MOS or job position.
why: Specified duties are those related to jobs and positions.
Directed duties are not specified as part of a job position or MOS and are other-directed.
Individual responsibility is a category of responsibility, not a type of duty.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines Command Responsibility?
questions.key: Collective or organizational accountability, including how well the unit performs its missions
distractors: Every soldier's responsibility to perform his duty to the best of his ability and to improve his performance
The authority leaders have over soldiers by virtue of rank or assignment
The authority extended to all soldiers to act in the absence of a unit leader
questions.explanation: Responsibilities fall into two categories; command responsibility is collective or organizational accountability and covers how well the unit performs its missions.
why: That defines individual responsibility.
That defines command authority.
That defines general military authority.

questions.stem: In the absence of a unit leader or other designated authority, a soldier takes action at an incident. Which type of authority allows this?
questions.explanation: General military authority is extended to all soldiers to take action and act in the absence of a unit leader or other designated authority.
why: Command authority comes from rank or assignment over soldiers in a chain of command.
Command responsibility is collective accountability for unit performance, not an authority.
Individual responsibility is each soldier's duty to perform to the best of his ability.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines authority?
questions.key: The legitimate power or right to command, make decisions, and enforce obedience within the military hierarchy
distractors: The legally established and moral obligation a soldier assumes for his own actions, accomplishments and failure
The specific tasks or assignments that individuals within the Philippine Army perform
Systematic evaluations to ensure units, personnel and equipment adhere to standards and regulations
questions.explanation: Slide 28 defines authority as the legitimate power or right to command, make decisions and enforce obedience, typically delegated by rank and position.
why: That defines responsibility.
That defines duties.
That defines inspections.

questions.stem: Which list contains the two categories of inspections for determining the status of individual soldiers and their equipment?
questions.explanation: Slide 32 gives two categories: in-ranks inspection, done in unit formation, and in-quarters (barracks) inspection.
why: On-the-spot inspection is an informal, unscheduled check, not one of the two categories listed.
Pre-combat inspections are a readiness check, not one of the two categories listed.
Neither on-the-spot nor pre-combat inspection is one of the two categories.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines Corrections?
questions.key: Actions taken to address deficiencies, errors, or violations identified during inspections or through other means
distractors: Systematic evaluations to ensure units, personnel, equipment and facilities adhere to standards and regulations
An informal, unscheduled check of equipment, soldiers, or quarters
The legally established and moral obligation a soldier assumes for his own actions
questions.explanation: Corrections are actions taken to address deficiencies identified during inspections or other means, to maintain standards and foster accountability.
why: That defines inspections.
That is an on-the-spot inspection.
That defines responsibility.

questions.stem: A sergeant makes an informal, unscheduled check of a soldier's equipment and quarters. Which of the following does this describe?
questions.explanation: Making an informal, unscheduled check of equipment, soldiers or quarters is called an on-the-spot inspection.
why: An in-ranks inspection is done on personnel and equipment in a unit formation.
Pre-combat inspections confirm leaders and soldiers are prepared to execute operations and training.
On-the-spot correction is a corrective measure applied to a soldier's deficiency.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the on-the-spot correction steps?
questions.key: Dump every deficiency on the soldier in one session
distractors: Attack the performance, never the person
Don't keep bringing it up; when the correction is over, it is over
questions.explanation: Slides 33 and 36 list the steps: correct the soldier, attack the performance and never the person, give one correction at a time (do not dump), and do not keep bringing it up once the correction is over.
why: This is a listed step.
This is a listed step.
This is a listed step.

questions.stem: It is a vital component of the organizational structure that facilitates communication, leadership and support among enlisted personnel, and complements the formal chain of command.
questions.explanation: The NCO support channel complements the chain of command by addressing the needs of enlisted personnel and promoting morale, cohesion and unit effectiveness.
why: The chain of command is the formal channel the NCO channel complements.
The NCO professional development program is something the channel administers, not the channel itself.
Command authority is authority over soldiers by rank or assignment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the NCO support channel?
questions.explanation: The NCO support channel runs from the Command Sergeant Major through first sergeant, platoon sergeants, section and squad leaders, and team leaders. The company commander is an officer in the chain of command.
why: First sergeant is in the support channel.
Platoon sergeants are in the support channel.
Squad leaders are in the support channel.

questions.stem: A newly assigned NCO asks who his immediate leader is, what that leader expects of him, and what the strengths and weaknesses of his soldiers are. Which topic does this fall under?
questions.explanation: These are among the questions listed on slides 15 to 17 to consider when assuming a leadership position.
why: Inspections and corrections concern evaluating and correcting standards.
The NCO support channel concerns how NCOs assist the chain of command.
Duties, responsibilities and authority define tasks, obligations and the right to command.
